content.text: In investigating this issue, I was able to find the following F3 object with `placeTerm type="text" script="Latn"` XML attributes.
PID of example F3 object: "1711.dl:VQ4WDCSKQWMV38D"
After migrating that single PID with migration-utils, the diff of the source F3 "BIB0.0" datastream byte-for-byte matches the migrated datastream.
I wonder if the F3 HTTP API is actually the culprit of the observed XML transformation noted in this ticket.
Unfortunately, I am not currently in a position to verify this F3 hypothesis.
"Stopping" work on this ticket, pending input from

The problem appears when migrating inline datastreams.  In my test case, I compared the inline datastream in the test object stored on the filesystem in the Akubra structure with the OCFL versioned file of the same datastream (i.e., a direct file-to-file comparison).  The two files differed as described above.
I then downloaded the same source datastream using the Fedora 3 API, and compared it to the OCFL versioned datastream, and the two were identical.  Which shows, as
surmises, that Fedora 3 is transforming the stored XML during delivery.

So the question is:  which should be considered the canonical version of the inline XML datastream?  The version stored on disk, or the version delivered by Fedora through its API?  If the former, then OCFL contents should match the disk version, and this bug stands;  if the latter, then this issue is not a real bug, and can be closed.

I lean towards the stored version, but I could be talked out of that.  The stored F3 version is the version that matches the original ingested XML datastream, and as such, could be considered the "truer" version to the original (pre-Fedora) source.
This appears to be the source of the issue:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/migration-utils/blob/master/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/migration/foxml/FoxmlInputStreamFedoraObjectProcessor.java#L313-L331

It may be that the transformation is happening on the way out, and not on the way in.  One approach may be to create a StringBuffer object, then as each event is processed, write the raw data read in to the string buffer, and output that as the OCFL XML file.  A similar approach is demonstrated here:
http://groovyjavathoughts.blogspot.com/2011/04/using-stax-to-extract-records-from-xml.html
As a brief follow-up, the `StartElementEvent` created by the `XMLEventReader`, stores attributes in a HashMap, which has no guarantees around ordering.
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/migration-utils/blob/master/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/migration/foxml/FoxmlInputStreamFedoraObjectProcessor.java#L313-L331
My next exploration will be:
1. Can we get ordered attributes from the 'XMLStreamReader'?, otherwise
2. Can we inject our own implementation of `StartElementEvent` into the `XMLEventReader` flow?
Although a byte-for-byte migration is ideal, this issue of swapping the order of XML attributes is likely not a Beta-blocker. Moving to "minor".
I just setup an integration test for this, and, of course, the problem does not appear.
There are two issues here.
1. The inline xml is being read by a DOM parser which does not guarantee attribute order.
2. Fedora 3 modifies the xml before calculating the digest:
https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo-historical/blob/e8a3be191cce6bbf8f55cd02bf1d52ac53425146/fcrepo-server/src/main/java/fedora/server/storage/types/DatastreamXMLMetadata.java#L92

I have an uncontroversial solution for issue 1. However, if we want the migrated xml to match the recorded digest, then we will need to migrate the version of the xml that the above linked code produces.
Do we want to do this?
Example of transformed xml:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><rdf:RDF xmlns:fedora-model="info:fedora/fedora-system:def/model#" xmlns:rdf="
http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#

"><rdf:Description rdf:about="info:fedora/1711.dl:CModelAudioStream"><hasModel rdf:resource="info:fedora/fedora-system:ContentModel-3.0" xmlns="info:fedora/fedora-system:def/model#"/></rdf:Description></rdf:RDF>
I think the OCFL xml file should be a copy of the inline xml that is stored on disk in the FOXML file, not transformed in any way by Fedora 3 or the migration utility.

This raises a problem for checksum comparison, as Fedora 3 transforms the stored inline XML prior to calculating and recording, then verifying the checksum.  This means that what is stored in OCFL will have a different checksum than the one recorded in the Fedora 3 datastream record.  I'm okay with that.  The differences can be accounted for as part of a validation process, separate from the migration process.
https://github.com/fcrepo-exts/migration-utils/pull/141
Resolved with
https://github.com/fcrepo-exts/migration-utils/commit/9955b0adf331f028aa16a8dcc84b36ad97a88642
Inline XML datastreams migrated from Fedora 3.x to OCFL currently undergo transformations:  attributes are rearranged; XML entities are resolved to characters.  Example:

diff <(curl -qs http://localhost:9090/fedora/objects/1711.dl:TESTMIGRATEOBJ/datastreams/TEST1/content) /var/tmp/ocfl/ocfl/1711.dl%3aTESTMIGRATEOBJ/v4/content/TEST1
17c17
< <placeTerm script="Latn" type="text">New York</placeTerm>
---
> <placeTerm type="text" script="Latn">New York</placeTerm>
20c20
< <placeTerm script="Latn" type="text">Chicago</placeTerm>
---
> <placeTerm type="text" script="Latn">Chicago</placeTerm>
23c23
< <placeTerm script="Latn" type="text">Toronto, Canada</placeTerm>
---
> <placeTerm type="text" script="Latn">Toronto, Canada</placeTerm>
29c29
< <placeTerm script="Latn" type="text">Sydney, Australia</placeTerm>
---
> <placeTerm type="text" script="Latn">Sydney, Australia</placeTerm>
35c35
< <placeTerm script="Latn" type="text">London, UK</placeTerm>
---
> <placeTerm type="text" script="Latn">London, UK</placeTerm>
39c39
< <dateOther encoding="w3cdtf" keyDate="yes">1913</dateOther>
---
> <dateOther keyDate="yes" encoding="w3cdtf">1913</dateOther>
62c62
< <topic>Choruses (Men's voices, 4 parts)</topic>
---
> <topic>Choruses (Men's voices, 4 parts)</topic>
70c70
< <accessCondition type="useAndReproduction" xlink:href="http://rightsstatements.org/vocab/NoC-US/1.0/">No copyright - United States</accessCondition>
---
> <accessCondition xlink:href="http://rightsstatements.org/vocab/NoC-US/1.0/" type="useAndReproduction">No copyright - United States</accessCondition>
Inline XML should be migrated the same way as managed datastreams:  an exact byte-for-byte copy of the inline XML should be written to the OCFL file.
